findings.text: Using reflect.TypeOf(list).Kind() instead of listValue.Kind() causes a panic when list is an untyped nil (reflect.TypeOf(nil) returns nil, calling .Kind() on nil panics). Additionally, for typed nils like ([]int)(nil), the kind check passes (returns Slice) but subsequent listValue.MapKeys() or listValue.String() calls will panic on the invalid Value, breaking the original graceful nil handling.
